pr_title: Always fill passed in buffer in StreamFillBufferExtensions
pr_body:
The returned `byte[]` was always correct, but the passed-in `buffer` argument was not being filled correctly when there were multiple reads since it was effectively turned into a scratch buffer. This caused some flakiness in older tests.

I've change all the methods to not return `byte[]` and changed all the callsites using the returned `byte[]` to use the passed-in `buffer` instead to keep the implementation simpler and to reduce the likelihood that it ever goes into a half-broken state again.

Fixes #34992
Fixes #34947

review_comments: I figured I'd just stick it in this PR because it's not big enough for its own. Look at line 701.

I'm using `ReadAtLeastLengthAsync` on purpose. I don't want to read an exact amount. I want stream to give me the expected amount of data but leave the door open to the stream returning more.

There is a bug in HttpClient's response stream that only shows up when you call ReadAsync and ask to read more data that is available.

I know. That's not this test though. I kept your test demonstrating the bug in HttpClient's response stream passing in a larger buffer than needed. See [here](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/35003/files#diff-69bd98bd920bf41ec1df4627369cfb21d6429e4c6eb75255a8b64b5a0d7476a7R217). I don't see the benefit of returning the buffer rather than passing it in. The caller usually has a better idea of the appropriate buffer size and it doesn't really complicate the call sites.
